glm.feedback:
## Review

The diff is a substantial, well-tested implementation that largely matches the (heavily self-documenting) spec: the envelope grammar, activation record, mint/gate hooks, `hooks-codex` registration, launcher env-injection, helper CLI, docs delta, and hook-inventory audit are all present and mutually consistent. The fail-open contract, mint-once/consume-once exclusivity, compound-command smuggling closures, and test quality are genuinely good. Below are the defects I found.

### Findings

- Category: bug
  Severity: medium
  File: `plugins/shipwright-iterate/scripts/hooks/codex_pretooluse_matcher.py` — `_SHELL_OPERATORS` (~line 22) and the accepted-risk comment in `_segment_targets_setup`
  Finding: Redirection is not handled: with `punctuation_chars=True`, shlex emits `>`, `<`, `(`, `)` as standalone tokens, but `_SHELL_OPERATORS` only contains `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `&`, and `_UNSAFE_SUBSTRINGS` doesn't cover them. So `uv run setup_iterate_worktree.py > ~/.bashrc` is a single segment whose program matches the wrapper check → **allowed** while armed-and-unsettled, and the docstring's claim that trailing tokens "can't smuggle a SECOND command past the gate (that still needs a shell operator)" is false — `>` is a shell operator that writes to an arbitrary path.
  Suggestion: Treat `>`, `<`, `(`, `)` (tokens arriving via `punctuation_chars`) as deny conditions alongside `|`/`||`, or add them to `_UNSAFE_SUBSTRINGS`; add a regression test for `uv run setup_iterate_worktree.py > <file>`.

- Category: bug
  Severity: medium
  File: `plugins/shipwright-iterate/scripts/hooks/codex_pretooluse_matcher.py` — `_segment_targets_setup`, `uv`-wrapper loop
  Finding: Flag parsing skips `-`-prefixed tokens but not their **values**: `uv run --project-root . setup_iterate_worktree.py` consumes `.` (the flag's value) as the target position → no match → **deny** of a legitimate invocation shape. This is exactly the "false-deny on legitimate variants" class the internal plan review's finding 11 required the matcher to avoid; the shipped hint happens to place flags after the script, but `uv run --project <path> <script>` is common real usage.
  Suggestion: Either restrict the wrapper path to `uv run [flags-without-values] <target>` and deny anything else (fail toward deny, consistent with the matrix), or parse known value-taking flags (`--project`, `--project-root`, `--with`, `--directory`, `--no-sync` is value-less, etc.) explicitly.

- Category: bug
  Severity: medium
  File: `plugins/shipwright-iterate/scripts/hooks/codex_activation_mint.py` and `plugins/shipwright-iterate/scripts/hooks/codex_pretooluse_gate.py` — `_resolve_project_root(cwd)` call sites in `handle_payload`
  Finding: The doubt-review "FIXED" claim in `hook-inventory.md` ("mint()/consume() now short-circuit on a plain `Path.exists()` check… collapsing the cost… to 'once, on the single call that actually settles'") is **not achieved at the hook level**: both hooks call `_resolve_project_root(cwd)` — i.e. `normalize_cwd()`, a git subprocess — on *every* invocation, *before* the library's exists() short-circuit can run. Every `PreToolUse` call in an armed Codex session still spawns a git process for the whole session, which is precisely the cost the doubt review flagged.
  Suggestion: Move the exists()-style short-circuit above the normalize (e.g., cache per-session project_root keyed on raw cwd, or make the `.consumed` existence check reachable before normalization), or correct the inventory's "FIXED" claim to state the residual per-call git cost honestly.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: `shared/scripts/lib/codex_activation_record.py` — `_exclusive_create` (`path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` before the `try`)
  Finding: The `mkdir` call is outside the OSError guard, so an unwritable/read-only project root makes `mint()`/`consume()` **raise**, violating the module docstring's hard contract ("fail-open… never an exception"). The hooks' `main()` blanket `except` masks it in production, but direct library consumers (and the documented contract) are exposed.
  Suggestion: Wrap the `mkdir` in the same `try: … except OSError: return None` as the `os.open`, or use `_exists_fail_open`-style suppression.

- Category: spec
  Severity: low
  File: `.shipwright/planning/iterate/.../mini-plan.md` §1 "Edit" list and §2 step 8; `iterate-spec.md` AC0
  Finding: The mini-plan still instructs wiring the new hooks into `plugins/shipwright-iterate/hooks/hooks.json` (step 8: "Wire into `plugins/shipwright-iterate/hooks/hooks.json`"), but the diff (correctly, per the mid-run design pushback) wires via the new `hooks-codex/hooks.json`. The split is documented in `hook-inventory.md` and `docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md`, but the mini-plan text was never corrected — a future reader following it re-registers the gate for Claude, reintroducing the per-call Claude cost the split exists to prevent. AC0's text also still says "any of the three new hooks" although the Stop-gate cut leaves two.
  Suggestion: Add a one-line correction to mini-plan §1/step 8 pointing at the `hooks-codex` registration (the run's own convention for post-hoc plan corrections), and fix the "three" count in AC0.

- Category: test
  Severity: low
  File: `.shipwright/planning/iterate/.../iterate-spec.md` — Verification section; new tests under `shared/scripts/tools/tests/`
  Finding: The spec's verification commands cover only two test roots (`shared/tests` and `plugins/shipwright-iterate/tests`), but this run added tests in a third root: `test_codex_activation_helper.py`, `test_codex_activation_helper_guards.py`, `test_codex_hook_inventory_runtime_scope.py`, plus launcher/fixture changes in `shared/scripts/tools/tests/`. Those tests are never invoked by the recorded runner commands, so the run's own verification record doesn't execute a whole AC-bearing component's (Step 7 helper, launcher injection, merge) test coverage. (The round-2 spec-review already noted the missing matcher file; this is the same gap one size larger.)
  Suggestion: Add the `shared/scripts/tools/tests` invocation (or a `-k` selector for the new files) to the Verification section's runner commands.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: `plugins/shipwright-iterate/scripts/hooks/codex_activation_mint.py` — `main()`'s blanket `except Exception: return 0` combined with the gate's absent-record path
  Finding: If the mint hook fails (any exception → silent exit 0), the gate sees an absent record and silently allows with no visibility — the unarmed-warning path only covers the minted `armed: false` record, not "mint never happened". This is acknowledged in `spec_review_reply.json` as judged faithful to the AC's scope, so I record it only because the spec's stated intent is "the fail-open default is never silent".
  Suggestion: Either accept and document it in the docs section (one sentence), or have the gate treat "no record at all in a Shipwright project under Codex" the same as unarmed on first consume.

### Non-findings I checked and cleared

`parse()` never-raises contract (TypeError guard, charset-enforced single-line, two-match ambiguity), compose's `\Z` anchoring (with a dedicated trailing-newline regression test), session_id path-traversal sanitization, the `.bat`/`.cmd` shim refusal (with an empirical Windows probe), the launcher env-injection quoting (Windows `set "VAR=..."` + POSIX shlex.quote), the `cmd_resolver` dedup (RuntimeError preserved), the `_load_hooks` merge additivity (both matchers survive, no-codex-file no-op), and the concurrent-consume exactly-one-wins test are all correct.

### Overall assessment

The mechanism is sound and matches the spec's corrected (post-Architecture-Review) scope; the two matcher gaps (redirection allow, flag-value false-deny) and the false "cost collapsed" claim are the items I'd fix before merge — all are small, local, and test-coverable. Ship-with-fixes.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
